hypotheses.paper: Sigma a singular S^2-manifold homeomorphic to a sphere with s >= 3 conical singularities of respective angles theta_i (l.1930)
hypotheses.note: GX.IsConeSphere M theta p: a singular (SO(3), S^2)-manifold M homeomorphic to S^2, distinct points p_i, each a cone point of angle theta_i (GX.IsConePoint: gx's X_theta-chart, def:atlas l.1905, for the family of spherical cones C_theta), no other singular point. s >= 3 is part of TroyanovAngleCondition. An angle 2pi marks a regular point (finding 1).

hypotheses.paper: Troyanov's theorem (MR1005085): such a surface exists
hypotheses.note: GX.TroyanovTheorem, a Prop; its proof GX.troyanovTheorem is a tagged sorry (DEC-136, target T-gx-troyanov).

hypotheses.paper: the Thurston suspension M of Sigma is a singular (SO(4), S^3)-manifold (l.1931, 'or check that directly')
hypotheses.note: built and proved: GX.thurstonSuspension = GX.thurstonStructure sph2Base M, the maximal a.e. atlas generated by the cone charts; GX.isAEAtlas_thurstonAtlas (chart changes in SO(4) via 1 + A, support portly by prop:susp_portly), 0 sorry. Reading of the radius: SCOPE (b) of S3Model (question 1).

hypotheses.paper: the angles theta_i are well defined (implicit in 'conical singularities of respective angles theta_i')
hypotheses.note: proved: GX.IsConePoint.angle_eq and GX.IsConeSphere.isConePoint_iff, from GX.sphCone_eq_of_iso (an a.e. isomorphism of open subsets of C_theta, C_theta' whose domain contains the apex of C_theta, theta != 2pi, forces theta = theta'), 0 sorry; the connectedness of the open sets in def:family_singular_manifolds_endowed is not used (weakened).

hypotheses.note: pairwise distinct angles, as DEC-69 read it for GX.TroyanovSuspensionTheorem.

hypotheses.paper: the facts of l.1933-1935 (Aut, rigidity near O, rotations about the axes, analyticity iff S = {O})
hypotheses.note: GX.ThurstonCexFacts: Sing(susp Sigma) = O and the rays over the p_i of angle != 2pi; DEC-69's SuspensionCexFacts at O. GX.thurstonSuspensionFacts is a tagged sorry (target T-gx-troyanov-suspension). The conclusion (M, S) analytic iff S = {O} follows with 0 sorry (GX.cex_start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic_S3).

sorries.obstruction: Troyanov's existence theorem for spherical cone metrics on S^2 with prescribed angles (MR1005085, cited at l.1930). DEC-136: to be proved in full; target T-gx-troyanov. The objects it needs (the cone C_theta, cone spheres) are built here; no cone sphere with s >= 3 genuine cone points is constructed yet (gluing spherical triangles, or the variational method).

The facts of l.1933-1937 for the Thurston suspension susp(Sigma): rays over singular points singular (as GX.ConicStructure.mk_mem_sing, for the Thurston atlas, compact link), O singular (closure of the singular rays); an isomorphism near O fixes O (the singular locus is a star at O, an arc elsewhere), is an isometry and induces an automorphism of Sigma, trivial for distinct angles; the rotations about a singular ray do not extend. Target T-gx-troyanov-suspension.

findings: Troyanov's condition as printed at l.1930 admits an angle theta_i = 2pi, which is not a conical singularity: (9pi/10, 19pi/20, pi, 2pi) satisfies it with pairwise distinct angles (GX.troyanovAngleCondition_two_pi, proved; it is DEC-69's witness with 2pi appended, which leaves the sum unchanged). The cex's 's >= 3 conical singularities of respective angles theta_i' must then read 's cone points, a 2pi one a marked regular point'. Harmless for the cex: the condition forces at least three angles != 2pi (GX.TroyanovAngleCondition.three_le_card_ne_two_pi, proved), so Sigma always has >= 3 genuine conical singularities. The author may want 'theta_i != 2pi' or 'theta_i in ]0, 2pi[ ∪ ]2pi, +inf[' in the cex.

The suspension of sec:susp (l.698-700), (M x R_+)/~ with metric dr^2 + sin(r)^2 g: with r over all of R_+, the metric degenerates at r = pi (and at every k*pi; it is locally spherical again on each band between), so (M x R_+)/~ with it is not a Riemannian (cone-)manifold; the intended model is r in [0, pi) (one centre) or [0, pi] with both ends collapsed (two centres). The cex (l.1931-1933: one centre O, singular locus 'homeomorphic to a line except at O') fits the open ball r < pi. Formalized: the open ball, parametrised by r' = tan(rho/2) in [0, inf) on GX.Susp (S3Model SCOPE (b)).
questions: Thurston's suspension (l.698-700) for spherical models: is r meant in [0, pi) (the open ball about O, one centre), or in [0, pi] with both ends collapsed (two centres)? Reading taken: [0, pi), realised on GX.Susp M (r' in [0, inf)) by rho = 2 arctan r'.

'Conical singularity of angle theta' (l.694, l.1930) is read in gx's framework as an X_theta-chart (def:atlas) for the family of spherical cones C_theta: an a.e. (SO(3), S^2)-isomorphism of a neighbourhood of x onto a connected neighbourhood of the apex of C_theta (GX.IsConePoint); 'metric space locally isometric to either of local models' is not formalized metrically (no Riemannian metric). Is that the intended notion? Note: the family (C_theta)_{theta>0}, S_theta = {apex}, is not an analytic family in the sense of l.1899 (S_{2pi} is not in sing C_{2pi} = empty; exists_aut unproved), so IsConePoint is def:atlas's chart condition without its standing hypothesis; for theta != 2pi the eq_of_iso half is proved (GX.sphCone_eq_of_iso).
'Generic Sigma' (l.1935) is read, as DEC-69 did, as 'the theta_i pairwise distinct' (the paper's instance at l.1933). Kept.

The paper's 'Aut(Sigma) -> Aut(M) is a group isomorphism' (l.1933) is not part of the stated facts (DEC-69's SuspensionCexFacts carries the local rigidity at O, which the cex's conclusion uses). Should the angle-tied statement also carry Aut(Sigma) = Aut(M)?

kb_proposals: The cone angle of a conical model is an invariant of the apex without the B21 lifting machinery: lift the isomorphism on a punctured neighbourhood through the covering exp : C -> C* (mathlib IsCoveringMapOn.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts on a convex strip of R^2), compare developing maps by rigidity (GX.exists_smul_eq_on_of_isLocalHomeomorphOn), and finish with an integer-valued continuous function (GX.eq_of_continuous_intValued); see GX.sphCone_exists_int_mul.

The spherical models are GX.RaySphere V with GX.SpecialOrth V (S3Model); S^3 = Sph3 = RaySphere (R + (R + C)), polar axes split off by GX.PolarSum, so the Thurston suspension S^n -> S^{n+1} is GX.thurstonStructure (cone charts through GX.sphConic, chart changes 1 + A via GX.liftSO).

A conical model in a non-Euclidean (G,X) is GX.polarCone: give an open embedding j : C -> X conjugating z -> e^{i alpha} z to some rho in G (for S^2: GX.stereoInv and GX.rotSO3); it ports GX.conical, apex singular iff alpha != 2pi.

To reuse GX.ConicStructure.mk_mem_sing (rays over singular points singular) for the Thurston atlas, the link action must be of a subgroup of SO(R + W): transport a singular (SO(W), S(W))-structure along GX.liftSO (IsGXAtlas, IsThinner only see the maps x -> g . x, so the transport is definitional chasing).
